transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-14 15:00 PDT | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jessie Li (Redwood Solutions), Jared Lim (CTO - Hightower), Sana Patel (Eng Manager), Anika Bose (Platform), Tom W. (SRE)
Link: https://redwood.zoom/meet/ff-20261014-HTWR

[00:00:00] Alice Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — we wanted to get a quick sense of your traffic shape and p95 goals so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. sound good?
[00:00:12] Jared Lim: yeah thanks, Alice. quick context: we're Hightower AI, we ship live summarization in our fleet ops product. normal steady state is about 120 concurrent streams, but when we onboard a big customer we see short bursts to ~1,200 simultaneous sessions for 2-6 minutes.
[00:00:28] Sana Patel: and most sessions are streaming token-by-token with partial updates — so p95 streaming latency matters more than raw throughput numbers. we target p95 <= 200ms on token arrival for our default model.
[00:00:41] Marco Ruiz: ok that p95 is a helpful anchor. couple clarifying q's: what's your typical prompt and response length? like average tokens in/out?
[00:00:48] Tom W.: average input is 45 tokens, generation ~150 tokens on average; heavy flows go to 600 tokens in some cases. token length distribution I can share after the call.
[00:00:59] Jessie Li: when you say streaming p95 200ms, is that p95 per token from request to first token on the wire, or p95 between tokens while streaming?
[00:01:08] Sana: mostly per-token latency while streaming, so tail between successive tokens matters. initial token is important too but the steady stream latency is our focus.
[00:01:18] Marco: got it. for that workload pattern we usually look at a few levers: continuous batching, KV cache hit rate for repeated prompts, and whether quantized variants of the model degrade quality too much. do you have an agreed quality threshold?
[00:01:31] Jared: we need less than 1.5% regression on ROUGE/L, something like that — we can provide eval sets.
[00:01:40] Alice: perfect. constraint-wise, do you require data residency or will a hosted endpoint be acceptable?
[00:01:47] Anika: security is the main ask — SOC2 compliance is a must, and for 2 of our top-tier customers they require VPC private deployment or at least dedicated tenancy. could you outline tradeoffs?
[00:01:58] Marco: briefly: Hosted is quickest to run, we have multi-tenant isolation, SOC2 and audit logs are standard. Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool for predictable p95 at scale and isolation; we can set autoscale and burst capacity. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict network controls — more ops but full control.
[00:02:16] Tom W.: what's the failover if Dedicated hits capacity? does Redwood fallback to a smaller model or to Hosted?
[00:02:24] Marco: we have smart routing policies — you can configure fallbacks to a smaller quantized variant in the same infra tier, or to Hosted as a last-resort cross-region fallback. we can also set circuit-breaker thresholds so you don't see huge errors.
[00:02:36] [00:02:40] Jared: question on quantization — our models are fairly sensitive to token-level coherence. do you have prior benchmarks on 8-bit / dynamic quant where streaming p95 is impacted?
[00:02:50] Marco: yes, we run per-model quantization profiles. in our catalog we show latency vs quality curves; sometimes 8-bit helps latency but adds slight perplexity increases. for streaming p95, 8-bit often reduces per-token time by 8-12% depending on kernel. but if your evals show quality drops over threshold we won't recommend it for production.
[00:03:10] Sana: how do you handle KV cache locality during bursts — does it stay warm across sessions?
[00:03:16] Marco: we have prefix and KV caching strategies; cache hit rate is heavily influenced by prompt reuse. we can pin warm instances for dedicated pools to keep KV cache warm across bursts — that reduces cold-start token penalties.
[00:03:29] Alice: would you consider a hybrid — Dedicated with a small Hosted overflow for peak spikes?
[00:03:33] Jared: yes that's what we're thinking — want predictable p95 during steady and a cost-effective overflow when spikes hit.
[00:03:40] Marco: we support that — routing policy can send to Dedicated, then to Hosted if the Dedicated pool is saturated. you can set cost or latency priority.
[00:03:47] [00:03:50] Tom W.: what's the cold-start penalty for a new Dedicated VM or kernel refresh? we saw previously a 800ms tail on cold LLM starts elsewhere.
[00:03:59] Marco: cold starts depend on model size and kernel warmers. we profile cold start per model; typically for the sizes you're describing a cold start ranges 200–600ms for the first token unless you pre-warm. Dedicated with pinned capacity eliminates most cold starts.
[00:04:15] Jared: for benchmarking, what's your recommended token/sec harness? we want reproducible p95 token latency and throughput numbers.
[00:04:22] Marco: we'll share a standard harness — we usually run streaming tests measuring per-token latency histogram at different concurrencies: 100, 300, 600, 1,200. we include varying token lengths and burst windows (2m, 5m, 10m) and KV cache hit scenarios.
transcript_continued:
[00:04:40] Jessie Li: small note — our test harness uses a combination of k6 for load shaping and a specialized client that measures first-byte and per-token timing. we'll open-source the template.
[00:04:52] Anika: on encryption — can you integrate with our KMS? we need customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated.
[00:05:00] Marco: yes, Dedicated and Private both support KMS integrations; Hosted can support envelope encryption with customer KMS depending on contract.
[00:05:07] Sana: SSO and RBAC — we need SAML SSO and granular RBAC for teams. how granular is RBAC in the console?
[00:05:13] Alice: console RBAC supports role bindings per team and per model-route; we can lock down model version rollouts and restrict who can change routing policies. SAML + SCIM provisioning is supported.
[00:05:23] Jared: another question — do you expose token-level cost breakdown per request? we need that for our finance quotas.
[00:05:29] Marco: yes — per-request token breakdown and cost attribution are in the Console; you can tag keys and routes to the cost center.
[00:05:36] [00:05:40] Tom W.: for the pilot, can we run on our VPC or do we need to send sample traffic to Hosted?
[00:05:46] Marco: we can do either. fastest path is Hosted benchmark using your prompt set; if you want VPC-hosted agents we can schedule a Private pilot but that adds ops time.
[00:05:57] Alice: to align expectations: pilot goals should be p95 at target concurrencies, token/sec throughput during bursts, and quality delta under your eval. we'll run a baseline on Hosted and then a Dedicated run to show differences.
[00:06:10] Sana: sounds good. SLA question: what p95 SLOs do you guarantee for Dedicated?
[00:06:16] Marco: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets per model profile; we typically guarantee p95 within X ms of published profile depending on commit. we'll share the SLO table with the pricing sheet.
[00:06:27] Jared: curious about cost math — how does ongoing cost scale with pinned GPUs vs burst usage?
[00:06:32] Alice: Dedicated is commit-based; you pay for reserved capacity (lower unit cost) and we have burst credits for peaks. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be costlier at steady high throughput. we'll include an example TCO in the pricing matrix for your expected token volumes.
[00:06:46] [00:06:50] Anika: anything else on compliance — audit logs, retention, and data deletion for customers who need DSR?
[00:06:55] Marco: audit logs + long-term retention is available as an add-on. data deletion and retention policies are configurable; for Private we can fully hand over retention controls.
[00:07:07] Jared: ok that helps. let's recap and call out next steps.
[00:07:12] Alice: recap: Alice to send pricing and SLO table; Marco to share benchmark harness and sample load scripts; Sana and Tom to send prompt set and traffic curve; schedule pilot 10/26 week. any blockers?
[00:07:25] Sana: none. one last nit — can you show us a sample fallback trace for when Dedicated overflows to Hosted? we want to see latency differences in a real trace.
[00:07:34] Marco: yes we'll include a sample trace and dashboard screenshot.
[00:07:38] Jared: thanks all. that's it from me.
[00:07:41] Alice: awesome, we'll follow up via email with the items. thanks everyone.
